Prevention: Keep the farm weed free as they can act as alternative hosts, such as solanum family crops.
Observe correct planting spacing of 1 m by 1 m to avoid over crowding of plants.
Conserve natural habitats to enhance indigenous natural enemies.
Avoid planting gooseberries next to infested field or crops.
When moving through the gooseberry orchard, start with the non-infested area before moving to infested area.
Monitoring: Look for webs on the underside of the leaves.
Look out for tiny red or brown oval shaped pest with 8 legs on the underneath of the leaves.
Check for clusters of yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaf which may appear chlorotic.
Look out for speckled mottled leaves.
Consider takinh action when 8-10 mites per leaf are seen.
Direct Control: Prune overcrowded plants and destroy the crop debris by burning.
Use overhead irrigation as it helps in drowning the mites and reduces their population.
Spray with neem extracts (500 grams of leaves in 5 litres of water).
